meta.description: Quality control for bottom-up proteomics across three levels -- instrument/raw-signal (mass accuracy, RT/iRT fit, FWHM, TIC vs injection time, % MS2 identified), identification/run (missed cleavages, charge states, PTM handling artifacts, contaminants), and experiment/quantitative (replicate correlation on log2, CV on the linear scale, completeness, MNAR-vs-MCAR missingness, PCA/batch, TMT channel balance, DIA q-values). Mandates inspecting raw signal before normalizing.

scientific_integrity.detail: No invented numbers, DOIs or PMIDs in the Skill or in any output; the PTXQC 20/35% ID-rate bins were confirmed in the PTXQC 1.1.5 YAML. One attribution is wrong: the '>1%' contaminant flag is PTXQC's user-defined MYCOPLASMA threshold, not its general contaminant metric (P2). The DIA-NN 'High precision halves median CV' claim was not verified.

practice_boundaries.detail: All five outputs are research-sample QC: no diagnosis, treatment or triage of an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: The core methods hold up when run: inspect before normalizing, CV on the linear scale or as geometric CV, global q-value filtering, and batch in the design. The batch wording is inconsistent (P2), but no output reached an invalid conclusion.

code_usability.detail: Every SKILL.md function parses and imports and ran on pandas 3.0.5 / sklearn 1.9. The example exits 0. PTXQC createReport and MSstatsTMT dataProcessPlotsTMT ran. The crash paths depend on the input (sample_info index, all-NaN rows, fewer than 5 samples) and are recorded as P1, but the code is runnable.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 2: code covers only matrix-level QC; Level 1/2 metrics, TMT balance, DIA q-values and the contaminant fraction are prose only, and the Skill never names which MaxQuant/DIA-NN column is un-normalised. Correctness 2: raw_sample_qc reports 0% missing on MaxQuant zeros; the PTXQC >1% claim is misattributed; the MSstatsTMT 'RAW' claim is false under the defaults. Appropriateness 3.

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 2: pca_batch_check raises cryptic TypeError/ValueError on a RangeIndex sample_info, all-NaN rows or fewer than 5 samples. Error reporting 2: the Common Errors table helps, but the code has no checks. Recoverability 3: read-only and idempotent.

performance_context.note: Token cost 2: a 276-line, 25.7 KB SKILL.md is loaded whole, including Level-1 prose that cannot be executed and 13 references. Efficiency 3: StandardScaler is fitted twice, and abundance_bins is dead code.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 3: the funnel and ordering are very clear, but column mapping needs outside knowledge. Consistency 3: the '2-3x below group median' rule versus the example's total-signal <0.5x; 'never let batch dominate' versus 'batch in design'. Feedback 2: no QC-report or exclusion-decision template. Error prevention 3: strong failure-mode section, but it misses MaxQuant 0 = missing and LFQ = already normalised.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 4: natural triggers ('assessing data quality, diagnosing outlier samples, deciding which samples to exclude'). Forgiveness 2: no input requirements are stated (NaN for missing, sample-indexed annotation), and wrong input is computed silently instead of rejected.

security.note: Credential safety 4 (none needed). Input validation 2 (none, as in the shared template; no eval/exec). Data safety 4 (read-only; the example writes nothing).

maintainability.note: Modularity 3: small single-purpose functions, all inline in SKILL.md. Modifiability 3: thresholds kept in one table. Testability 3: one seeded example that runs offline, but no per-function tests.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision 4: explicit routing to quantification, differential-abundance and dia-analysis. Progressive disclosure 2: no references/ folder; everything is in SKILL.md. Composability 3: DataFrame in, DataFrame out, related Skills exist. Idempotency 4. Escape hatches 2: routing lines only; no stop conditions (n<5, no raw column available, exclusion sign-off by the human).

inputs.label: QC a MaxQuant LFQ run (8 samples, 2 batches) before limma
inputs.note: Contaminant rows stripped (60); contaminants 4.2-6.5% of raw Intensity; no loading failure; within-group r 0.956-0.966; linear CV 24%; MNAR profile; batch is PC1 (p<1e-4) and condition is PC2. Needed three adaptations: 0->NaN, sample-indexed annotation, completeness filter before PCA. PTXQC report produced.

assertions.text: raw_sample_qc as written reports per-sample ID counts and missing fraction that differ between samples on MaxQuant input
assertions.note: MaxQuant stores missing as 0; the verbatim function returned n_quantified=1500 and missing_pct=0.0 for all 8 samples

assertions.text: pca_batch_check runs on sample_info as loaded from sample_annotation.csv

assertions.text: Batch is detected as the dominant axis and a design-level remedy is recommended before testing

key_strengths: The inspect-before-normalize principle proved correct when run: median centring set all 8 log2 medians to 0 on the failed file and erased the T4 deficit that raw Intensity total signal (0.41x) exposed
Global q-value guidance is right and effective: requiring Global.Q.Value and Global.PG.Q.Value <= 0.01 removed all 60 groups that pass only run-level q
CV guidance is correct: geometric CV from log2 (25.0%) matches linear CV (24.3%), while the base formula on log2 gives 1.4%
Explicit scope routing to quantification, differential-abundance and dia-analysis; all six related Skills exist, and the seeded example runs offline
The PTXQC route works as described: createReport(txt_folder=) ran on a minimal two-file folder and skipped the missing tables with warnings

recommendations.title: raw_sample_qc counts MaxQuant zeros as quantified
recommendations.problem: The verbatim function returned 1500 IDs and 0% missing for every sample, which hides T4's 19% ID drop and 31% missingness on the failed file.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill never states that MaxQuant writes missing values as 0 (and that DIA-NN PG.MaxLFQ can be 0).
recommendations.fix: Add `raw_intensities = raw_intensities.replace(0, np.nan)` inside raw_sample_qc and state in the Inspect section that search-engine zeros are missing values.

recommendations.title: Un-normalised column never named per tool
recommendations.problem: On MaxQuant 'LFQ intensity' the 3x-low T4 is 1.02x (total) and 1.41x (median) and is never flagged; only 'Intensity' shows 0.41x. The rule's median-versus-total choice also decides the flag (0.62x versus 0.41x).
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill says 'un-normalized matrix' without mapping it to MaxQuant, DIA-NN or TMT columns, and gives no ID-count threshold.
recommendations.fix: State: MaxQuant 'Intensity <s>' (LFQ is already MaxLFQ-normalised); DIA-NN Precursor.Quantity (not Precursor.Normalised or PG.MaxLFQ). Apply the 2x rule to total signal and flag an ID count more than 15-20% below the group median.

recommendations.title: pca_batch_check crashes or misplaces samples
recommendations.problem: Cryptic TypeError with a RangeIndex sample_info; ValueError on all-NaN rows; ValueError at n<5; row-median fill pulled the failed T4 to the centre of the PCA.
recommendations.root_cause: Hard-coded n_components=5, no index/NaN checks, and median imputation that makes high-missing samples look average.
recommendations.fix: Require sample_info indexed by sample (assert set equality), dropna(how='all'), use n_components=min(5, n_samples-1), and run PCA on complete cases or with a low-value fill, noting the imputation bias.

recommendations.title: MSstatsTMT QC plot is post-normalisation by default
recommendations.problem: dataProcessPlotsTMT after default proteinSummarization showed all 20 channel medians at 24.73, which contradicts the Skill's 'on RAW reporter intensities' and hides channel imbalance.
recommendations.root_cause: proteinSummarization(global_norm=TRUE) is the default, the Skill does not mention it, and the tool needs PSM-level input.
recommendations.fix: Say proteinSummarization(..., global_norm=FALSE, reference_norm=FALSE) for the balance view and add a pandas within-plex channel-total check (fold versus plex median, >2x investigate).

recommendations.title: PTXQC '>1%' contaminant flag misattributed
recommendations.problem: The synthetic run has 4.2-6.5% contaminant intensity, so every sample trips the Skill's '>1%' rule; in PTXQC 1.1.5 the 1% threshold belongs to the user-defined MYCOPLASMA SpecialContaminants plot.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill conflates PTXQC's SpecialContaminants default with its continuous general contaminant score.
recommendations.fix: Replace it with a lab-baseline control-chart statement and a group-difference check, and add a code line computing the contaminant fraction per sample.

recommendations.title: Dead code and a scale-dependent '~14x' claim
recommendations.problem: missingness_profile computes abundance_bins and discards it. Base-CV-on-log2 compression measured 16.9-17.1x at mean log2 24.7; it scales with about ln2 x mean log2.
recommendations.root_cause: Code drift and a constant quoted for a quantity that depends on intensity units.
recommendations.fix: Return the per-bin present fraction from missingness_profile, and word the claim as 'about 15-20x at typical MaxQuant intensities (scale-dependent)'.

recommendations.title: Batch guidance and output template inconsistent
recommendations.problem: 'Never let batch be the dominant axis going into differential testing' cannot be met by 'include batch in the design', which leaves the PCA unchanged. DIA, TMT and Level 1/2 have no code and there is no QC-report template.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill mixes matrix correction and model-based adjustment and ends sections with routing lines instead of deliverables.
recommendations.fix: Recommend limma::removeBatchEffect for plots only plus batch in the design for the test; add a QC-summary and exclusion-decision table template, and stop conditions (n<5, no raw column available, human sign-off on exclusions).
